drills.name: Wh-answer chain
drills.spec: Beat at 60bpm. English cue, learner answers aloud in Japanese, native audio confirms. 'Who's there?' > Dare ga iru? | 'A friend.' > Tomodachi ga iru. | 'What's there?' > Nani ga aru? | 'A key.' > Kagi ga aru. | 'Who ate it?' > Dare ga tabeta? | 'The kid did.' > Kodomo ga tabeta. Twelve cues, no wa anywhere in the run.
drills.target: 12/12 with ga on both question and answer, no hesitation over one beat.

drills.name: Star rejection
drills.spec: Audio plays a mix of good and bad strings; learner says 'nai' (bad) or 'aru' (good) on the beat. Bad: *Dare wa iru. *Nani wa aru. *Dare wa tabeta. Good: Dare ga iru. Neko wa iru. Neko wa doko? Eki wa doko? This is the only negative evidence the learner will ever get for bare wa; run it every day of the six-day unit.
drills.target: 18/20, and zero false 'good' on any *dare wa item.

drills.name: ni / de switch
drills.spec: One place noun, two predicates, alternating on the beat. kooen > kooen ni iru / kooen de asobu | uchi > uchi ni aru / uchi de taberu | mise > mise ni aru / mise de kau | heya > heya ni iru / heya de yomu | eki > eki ni iru / eki de matsu. Cue is the place noun plus English 'be' or 'do'.
drills.target: 20 switches, no particle error, under 90 seconds.

drills.name: Animacy sort
drills.spec: Rapid noun cue, learner supplies the right existence verb: neko > iru. kagi > aru. kodomo > iru. mizu > aru. tori > iru. kuruma > aru. sakana > iru. hako > aru. tomodachi > iru. densha > aru. Then the same list negative (inai / nai) and past (ita / atta).
drills.target: 30 items, 100% on the positive run, 28/30 across negative and past.

drills.name: Existence square
drills.spec: Four-cell grid called against the beat, animate row then inanimate row. iru / ita / inai / inakatta, then aru / atta / nai / nakatta. Cue is English tense plus polarity ('was not, animate'). Say aloud each round that aru's negative is nai, not *aranai.
drills.target: Both rows cold, 8 cells in under 12 seconds, accent correct ([0] row flat, [1] row falling).

drills.name: Particle strip
drills.spec: Native audio plays the careful version; learner immediately produces the stripped version, which is what gets graded. Yasai o taberu? > Yasai taberu? | Neko ga iru? > Neko iru? | Kagi ga atta? > Kagi atta? | Nani o suru? > Nani suru? | Kore ga wakaru? > Kore wakaru? Then reverse: stripped in, careful out.
drills.target: 10 pairs each direction; the stripped form must come out faster than the careful one.

drills.name: ga-object frame
drills.spec: Fixed frame 'watashi wa ___ ga ___', both slots swapped on the beat. Objects: neko, niku, yasai, uta, e, okane, mizu. Predicates: suki, kirai, daisuki, joozu, heta, hoshii, wakaru, dekiru. A stray o is called out on the spot.

drills.name: mo substitution
drills.spec: Sentence in, mo-version out. Neko ga iru > Neko mo iru. | Yasai o taberu > Yasai mo taberu. | Watashi wa suki > Watashi mo suki. | Kooen ni iru > Kooen ni mo iru. | Uchi de taberu > Uchi de mo taberu. Point out that wa/ga/o vanish under mo but ni/de survive.
drills.target: 15 items, correct deletion of wa/ga/o and correct retention of ni/de.

drills.name: tte yutta
drills.spec: Learner reports what the audio said. Audio 'Kooen ni iru.' > Kooen ni iru tte yutta. Audio 'Kagi ga nai.' > Kagi ga nai tte yutta. Then the imperfective: ... tte yutteta. Every production says yuu / yutta / yutteta; an 'itta' pronunciation is marked wrong immediately.

drills.name: Family row
drills.spec: English cue names referent and audience. 'your dad' > otoosan. 'my dad, to a stranger' > chichi. 'your mum' > okaasan. 'my mum' > haha. 'your older brother' > oniisan. 'my older brother' > ani. 'your older sister' > oneesan. 'my older sister' > ane. 'my or your younger sister' > imooto. 'my or your younger brother' > otooto. Always run the row complete, never one member alone.
drills.target: 10/10 on the in-group/out-group choice, every long vowel held full length (o-to-o-sa-N = 5 morae).

drills.name: Noun-ga accent
drills.spec: Accent pairs heard in the ga frame, learner calls the pattern. hana ga (flower [2], fall on ga) against flat [0] nouns tori ga, niwa ga, michi ga, yasai ga. Also kagi ga [2], kutsu ga [2], niku ga [2] against okane ga [0], tegami ga [0], kusuri ga [0]. Bare word first, then the ga frame, so the learner hears why the frame is required.
drills.target: 16/20 on the bare word, 20/20 in the ga frame.

drills.name: Two-mention narration
drills.spec: Learner narrates a scene twice over. First mention takes ga (Neko ga iru), every later mention takes wa (Neko wa isu no shita ni iru. Neko wa gohan o taberu). Prompts: a room, a park, a shop. Ungraded; run at the end of days 27, 35 and 42.
drills.target: First mention ga, later mentions wa, sustained over six or more sentences.
